tab_title: How To Set Up Blink Outdoor Camera
description:
Blink Outdoor Camera: https://amzn.to/3hbG62H
Favorite Smart Home Devices: https://www.amazon.com/shop/onehoursm...

In this video we teach you how to set up a Blink Outdoor Camera. The latest generation of Blink Outdoor Cameras are wifi video cameras that can operate up to 2 years on battery power. The Blink Outdoor camera also has the ability to be hardwired if prefer that over the battery power. The Blink camera system uses a wifi blink camera and a wifi base station which then converts the Blink video footage to a wifi signal so that the footage can be viewed on the cloud. The Blink Base station operates on wifi and just requires a plug for power, it does not need to be plugged into your modem or router. Multiple Blink cameras can be connected to one Blink Base station. A unique feature of the Blink Cameras and Blink Base station is that the Blink Base station has a USB port that allows you to locally record footage on a USB stick for free if you don't want to pay for cloud storage or if you want a local backup of your video footage.

How To Set Up Blink Outdoor Camera: 
1. Download the Blink app and create an account. 
2. Set up the Blink Base station first on the Blink app by scanning the QR code and following the instructions.  
3.  Once the base station is set up you can start installing the Blink Outdoor Camera. 
4. Use the included tool in the Blink Box and remove the rear cover from the Blink Outdoor Camera. Scan the QR code inside the Blink Camera to Install your Blink Outdoor Camera.
5. Insert the batteries into your Blink Camera. 
6. Reinstall the cover plate for your Blink Camera and secure with the provided tool.

transkript:
... A fabric is placed over the liner before the drainage box is inserted. Now we roll the liner up to the box so that we can fill and compact the gap around the drainage box. Next we start placing the rocks. I hand-picked and cleaned about 1.5 tons of sandstone. This will be the biggest rock. It forms the lowest weir and will be the central rock later. Since it is a wide weir stone, it must be installed nice and straight. Once it is in the right position, I look for rocks to go to the right and left of it. These will later ensure that the water does not flow to the sides of the center rock. Now we fold back the liner and model the next weir. Here we want to create a small waterfall. I have placed a flat red weir stone on top of two larger stones to create a greater difference in height. This will then be framed on both sides. Above it we want to build the next pool, for which I am modeling the riverbed accordingly. I make sure that all the cascades are designed differently and blend together. This will make the stream look more natural later on. I still need a bank edge made of taller rocks here. It's been raining a bit, and the liner is wet. So I'm using this blower tool to dry the liner before sealing the weirs with foam. I use the foam to glue the liner to the weir. This will ensure that the water flows smoothly over the rocks later. All used materials and tools are linked in the video description. The foam should only be used in the right places and in as little quantity as possible. Moss creates a natural look and is glued directly into the stone cracks with the foam. Now I can continue up here. We now move on to the spring. I have an idea on how I want it to look so lets see if I can get it done. It's like a puzzle every time since every rock is different. The water should feed the stream over this rock. ...

transkript: Hello here is Carl the landscape guy. In my new office I’m installing a split air conditioner system, that will be used for both heating and air conditioning. The model I chose is a 9,000 BTU 2.6 kw precharged inverter kit. Among other things, the manufacturer advertises that this system saves energy and is very quiet. It has an antibacterial coating on the fins, works with a new, environmentally friendly refrigerant and can be controlled via WLAN with a smartphone app. This system comes with the coolant prefilled unit, 9 feet of refrigerant piping, and small parts such as a feedthrough tube, insolation tape, sealant and rubber mounts. There is also the outer wall bracket, which I will show you later, when it comes to the assembly of the outside unit. Then here we have the indoor unit, which is very light. It comes with a cable that will connect both units. It also includes the manual, the remote control and a wall holder for it. Both devices seemed to have been well-packed and arrived undamaged. This is the back of the wall mount. The indoor unit will go on this brick and concrete wall. I measure the distance between the holes of the wall bracket from the outer edge of the unit. Horizontally, the plate is slightly adjustable. A minimum distance of half a foot from the ceiling must be kept so that the air can flow properly. I draw the height of the upper holes with the help of a level. The wall bracket can be easily detached from the plastic unit. It clips on at the bottom. I use the bracket to mark all holes exactly. I use a 5 mm masonry drill with a Bosch Hammer to make the holes. When drilling indoors I use the Kärcher wet & dry vacuum cleaner to catch most of the dust. In case you are interested, I will link all tools below in the video description. By the way, the rawl plugs and screws were not included. Now I will prepare to drill the 65mm hole in the wall. First I mark the position of the hole. You will find the distances for the hole in the installation manual, they are different for each unit. I use a long masonry drill to pre-drill the shank hole. I make sure that the hole is angled on a downward slope. When the guiding hole is all set, I set up the 65mm concrete shank drill bit and start making the hole little by little. Every few inches I empty out the drill. I drill from the inside out as far as I can get....

description:

Due to requests, I am now including links to products when possible. These links are provided for reference, no company or individual paid to be in this video.  Depending on the vendor, a small commission might be paid and if so, would be used to support continuing this channel.
Amazon Prime free 30-day trial: https://amzn.to/2U9pttN

More Teresa and YNH:    • Teresa Garrett - Do It Yourself, Quick Tip...  

Installing a walkway can be a very labor intensive job, but if you do it yourself, you can save a lot of money over hiring contractor.

Before you get started, you’ll need the following materials.
-fiber reinforced concrete
-claw hammer
-line level: https://amzn.to/2AxwsFX or https://amzn.to/3gYpxGL
-wooden stakes
-expansion joints: we used https://amzn.to/2A30IIX
-wood  forms
-trowel
-wheelbarrow
-Bosch electric shovel: https://amzn.to/2zSqJuy or manual equivalent 
-concrete mixing tools
-broom
-tape measure

First, determine how long and how wide you want your walkway to be. After you’ve measured the width, drive a stake into the ground on both sides of where you’ll begin, these stakes will be your reference points for the remainder of the project.

Then, attach a screw to the lower third of the first stake. Use a line level to make sure you’ve got the proper angle of drainage away from the house. 

The line level is basically a long piece of string strung through a small level. The string fits through two holes on top of the level, so you can slide the level along the string.

Take one end of the string, attach it to the screw you’ve installed on the first stake, drive a second stake at the end of your proposed walkway. Attach the other end of the string to this stake and check to make sure that you will have proper drainage. In other words, you don’t want the bubble to show “level”,you want there to be a slight slope away from the house. (Failure to make sure water will drain away from your house could later cause foundation problems) 

Next, use a shovel or the Bosch electric shovel, to dig out the area of  your walk. 

Once this is done, sink a stake about ever two feet on both sides of the cut out ground where your walkway will go. Then take 3” X 4’ pieces of plywood and attach them at ground level to the stakes. You can use a cordless screwdriver to hold the plywood to the stakes. These pieces of wood are your concrete forms which will hold the cement in place when you’re ready to pour the walkway.

But first, put in your expansion joints. Expansion joints are installed about every three feet and are used to keep your concrete from cracking during expansion and contraction in hot and cold weather.

Using fiber reinforced concrete, which we used in this segment, is a good idea. The hundreds of thousands of  tiny fibers give the concrete extra strength as is hardens, thereby eliminating the need for wire mesh or re-bar to support ordinary concrete.

Mix your concrete in a wheelbarrow. Then pour the walkway into the forms. Use a trowel to smooth it out and make sure you have a nice even finish. 

TIP: Before the concrete dries, use a broom to give the surface texture. Simply take a broom and lightly sweep across the concrete from side to side. This will put small grooves into the concrete surface as it dries and will reduce the chance of your walkway being slippery when wet.

After the concrete has thoroughly dried (usually five days) remove the outer forms and stakes and you’ve got a beautiful walkway.

WHAT WE USED

The material used to install the backyard sidewalk was Quikrete Fiber Reinforced Concrete.

Quikrete’s fiber reinforced concrete contains hundreds of  thousands of tiny fibers which finish smooth, eliminating the need for wire mesh or heavy re-bar in many slab-on-grade applications like walkways, patios steps etc. Specially developed to minimize cracking, chipping and flaking. 

Fiber reinforced concrete also dramatically reduces cracking caused by drying shrinkage.

Quikrete Expansion Joint Strips, https://amzn.to/2A30IIX protect concrete slabs from potential damage caused by expansion and contraction. Made from cane fiber, the five foot long strips are weather resistant, absorb very little water, and do not become brittle in cold weather.

tab_title: GE Top Load Washer Won't Drain or Spin
description:
GE top load washer won't drain or spin? Here's how I fixed a GE washer that won't drain by replacing the drain pump (model GTW220ACK3WW).
If your washer is full of water and the drain pump just hums, a jammed drain pump is a likely cause, and you can replace it yourself.

The lid lock engaged and the pump made a faint hum, so the lock was good and the pump was getting voltage. That was enough for me to skip meter readings at the pump and the control board. The tub can hold 8 to 26 gallons, so I emptied it with a 5-gallon shop vac first, then tipped the washer back. I took out the pump (three 3/8" hex screws), found the impeller jammed with sand, put in a new pump, checked for leaks, and tested it in service mode.

description:

If you need to repair your fan there are countless videos on YouTube covering repairs. In addition, you can find most user manuals of common fans online. This video just covers how to identify the most common noises to help you fix your fan.

tab_title: HOW IS THIS EVEN LEGAL?!?!
description:
This video is back up!! 
Here's why:
1) I try to treat people as I would like to be treated, and I would not want someone airing my dirty laundry to the world. However, I do think I would want to know this information if I were buying a knew home and knew nothing about the building industry. In an attempt to satisfy both concerns,  I have taken great care to make sure that the identity and location of the builder remained anonymous.  This isn't a personal attack on any single person or company. I am simply giving my PERSONAL opinion on why I would not invest my money in a house like this.
2) I think that homeowners should know what is going on INSIDE the walls of the biggest investment of their lives.  While I state in the video that the home is probably engineered and built to meet all local codes (I am not a structural engineer or building inspector), to me, the building details that a buyer can't see in a tour of the show home matter MORE than what you can see.  I can easily upgrade lighting, flooring, and cabinetry as budget permits, but if I am upgrading a poorly built structure, am I making a wise financial decision for the future?  Is it a good idea to invest all that material and capital into a building that will wind up in the landfill in 50 years?
Yes, the low end of the market is a tough place to compete.  However, it is possible to build a more comfortable, durable, efficient house for very little additional cost.  It would cost less than $2,500 to sheath this house in OSB and dramatically improve its structural rigidity, comfort and efficiency. tab_title: Just This ONE Remote Will Pair All Home Theater System Devices All-In-One (SofaBaton X1S Universal)
description:
SofaBaton X1S Smart Remote Review – One Remote to Control Your Entire Home Theater?
Tired of having a pile of remotes on your coffee table? In this video, we take a look at the SofaBaton X1S Universal Smart Remote Control, a programmable remote designed to bring your home theater equipment together under one controller.

The SofaBaton X1S is designed to control multiple entertainment devices, including televisions, AV receivers, soundbars, streaming devices, Blu-ray players, and other compatible equipment. Instead of juggling several remotes, you can program the X1S to manage your system from one place.

What Is the SofaBaton X1S Used For?
The X1S comes with a dedicated hub that communicates with compatible devices using infrared, Bluetooth, and supported network-based control methods. Because the hub sends infrared commands, you generally don't need to point the remote directly at your television or receiver.

You can also create custom activities that control several devices in sequence. For example, a movie-watching activity could turn on your TV, switch on your AV receiver, and select the appropriate inputs.

The system also supports compatible smart-home integrations, including Alexa and Google Assistant, allowing you to control supported activities using voice commands.

Strengths of the SofaBaton X1S
One remote for multiple devices: Consolidates compatible home theater equipment into one controller.

Hub-based infrared control: Place the hub where it can communicate with your equipment, even when the remote isn't pointed directly at the devices.

Custom activities and macros: Automate sequences of commands for watching television, movies, or listening to music.

Broad device compatibility: Supports many infrared devices and selected Bluetooth and network-controlled equipment.

Smart-home integration: Compatible setups can work with Alexa and Google Assistant.

Rechargeable design: Reduces the need to replace disposable batteries.

Customizable controls: Lets you organize device commands and activities around your entertainment setup.

Weaknesses of the SofaBaton X1S
Setup takes time: Programming devices, activities, and input sequences can require patience.

Compatibility isn't universal: Some Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and radio-frequency devices may not be supported, even if they work with other universal remotes.

Hub placement matters: Infrared commands need a clear path from the hub to the equipment, or suitable additional IR emitters.

Not every command is guaranteed: Some devices may require extra configuration, and certain commands may not be available in the database.

Dependence on software and connectivity: Configuration and some network-based features rely on the companion app, and certain smart functions depend on compatible network services.

Learning curve: Users who just want a basic replacement remote may find the setup and customization more complicated than necessary.

Price: It costs more than a simple universal remote, particularly if you only need to operate one or two devices.

Is the SofaBaton X1S Worth Buying?
The SofaBaton X1S is worth considering if you have a multi-device home theater and want to simplify everyday operation. Its hub, programmable activities, and multiple control methods make it more versatile than a basic infrared remote.

However, it isn't a perfect replacement for every original remote. Before buying, check compatibility with your exact TV, receiver, streaming box, and other equipment. You should also consider whether you really need hub-based control and programmable activities or whether a simpler remote would do the job.

Overall, the X1S is an interesting option for people who want greater control over their entertainment systems without keeping several remotes within reach. Its greatest strengths are flexibility and customization, while its main drawbacks are setup complexity and device compatibility limitations.

tab_title: How to Factory Reset ANY Dell Desktop or Laptop (OptiPlex XPS Workstation Tower All-In-One XPS 11 13
description:
How to Factory Reset Any Dell Desktop or Laptop (OptiPlex, All-In-One, XPS, Latitude, Inspiron, Vostro, Precision)
If your Dell computer is running slowly, has software problems, or you want to erase your personal data before selling it, performing a factory reset can restore Windows to its original state.
Before You Begin
Back up important files, photos, and documents.
Connect the computer to AC power.
Disconnect unnecessary USB devices.
Method 1: Reset Dell Using Windows Reset This PC
Windows 11
Click Start → Settings.
Select System → Recovery.
Under Recovery Options, click Reset PC.
Choose:
Keep my files (removes apps but keeps personal files)
Remove everything (complete factory reset)
Select:
Cloud Download (downloads fresh Windows files)
Local Reinstall (uses files already on the computer)
Follow the prompts and click Reset.
Windows 10
Click Start → Settings.
Select Update & Security.
Click Recovery.
Under Reset this PC, click Get Started.
Choose your preferred reset option.
Follow the on-screen instructions.
Method 2: Factory Reset When Windows Won't Start

Works on many Dell systems including:

Dell OptiPlex
Dell XPS
Dell Latitude
Dell Inspiron
Dell Vostro
Dell Precision
Dell All-In-One models
Steps
Turn the computer completely off.
Turn it on and repeatedly press F12.
Select SupportAssist OS Recovery if available.
Choose Restore System or Factory Reset.
Follow the prompts to reinstall Windows.
Method 3: Use Dell SupportAssist Recovery

Many newer Dell computers include Dell's recovery environment.

Power on the computer.
Press F12 repeatedly.
Select SupportAssist OS Recovery.
Choose Reset or Restore Factory Settings.
Follow the instructions.
Method 4: Reinstall Windows from a USB Drive

If recovery partitions are missing or damaged:

Download the Windows Media Creation Tool from Microsoft.
Create a bootable Windows USB drive.
Insert the USB drive into the Dell computer.
Press F12 during startup.
Select the USB device.
Install Windows and delete existing partitions if performing a complete reset.
Common Dell Models Covered
Dell OptiPlex desktops
Dell OptiPlex All-In-One
Dell XPS 13, XPS 15, XPS 17
Dell Latitude 11, 13, 14, 15
Dell Inspiron laptops and desktops
Dell Vostro systems
Dell Precision workstations
If the Reset Fails

Try:

Running Dell hardware diagnostics (F12 at startup)
Using SupportAssist Recovery
Reinstalling Windows from a USB drive
Replacing a failing hard drive or SSD if hardware errors are detected #dellvostro #dellrepair

1–3 Bags: Wheelbarrow / mixing tray

tab_title: Getting R-30 in an attic suite with 2x6 ceiling rafters
description:
UPDATE!!--- How's the foam doing 3 years later:     • Will rigid foam cause problems? My foam bo...  

Better than spray foam (thermal break and relatively consistent R-30+). Here's how to use 3 layers of 2 inch polyiso foam board to meet code and keep your new upstairs cozy.
**UPDATE WATCH THIS BEFORE YOU CUT FOAM    • What is the best tool for cutting foamboar...  
I used a 2 inch rigid polyiso foam (GAF Energyguard) I got from a local roofing supply company (ABC Roofing). It is really the type of foam they use on commercial roofs beneath a membrane. I believe mine was made by GAF, and ran me about $18 per 4x8' sheet. I cut two layers to fit in the rafter bays (so that's 4 inches), spaced 1&1/2" away from the roof-deck with scraps of 2x4s (which maxed out my 5 1/2" inch rafters). Then I put another layer across the rafters, which made a total of 6 inches of polyiso. Each inch was R-5.4, so the total R value of all 3 layers was 32.4. Wherever there were gaps, I squirted some Great Stuff in, then shaved the overflow back with a flush cut hand-saw.-- Yes, it passed insulation inspection.

If your system is around the 5-year mark and suddenly stopped blowing air while the outdoor condenser keeps running, you might be dealing with an internal electronic module failure—often accelerated by restrictive, high-MERV air filters.

How do you get rid of moles in your garden, and what actually works? After moles started destroying my lawn with molehills, I decided to test several different methods to see if I could stop them.

I tried castor oil as a natural mole repellent, using vibrations to scare the moles away, and even increasing how often my robotic lawnmower cut the grass. One of our cats also got involved!

After researching how mole tunnel systems work, including surface feeding tunnels, vertical shafts and deeper permanent runs, I realised where I'd been going wrong.

In this video, I'll show you what I tried, what failed, and the method that finally stopped the mole activity in my garden.

If you're dealing with molehills in your lawn and wondering whether mole repellents, vibration devices or mole traps actually work, hopefully my experience will save you some time and frustration.

tab_title: Is it Worth the Money? Froth-Pak Sealant 200 Spray Foam Insulation
description:
I bought this Froth-Pak 200 and tested it out for you, So you can see if it's something you want to buy and use yourself. This is their 200 soft kit closed cell insulation. It's a DIY friendly spray foam kit made to help seal the gaps and fill your wall cavities so everything is air tight and well insulated. 

Grab some Fort-Knox Co. gear, Visit my website: https://fortknoxcompany.com

I have done a lot of research on these kits and I decided to go with Froth-Pak specifically because they seemed to be the larger brand name and had better reviews overall. Also the projected sqft of spray per dollar was on the better value side.  None of the kits are "cheap" by any means, they all seem to be around $300 and up. So no matter what kit or brand you decide on you can plan to spend a few hundred at minimum. 

The set up was very easy, just like it said. No tricks, straight forward. Just a couple things to look out for or pay attention to. I noted them in the video after I sprayed the whole contents. It is a very diy friendly kit and can be easy to get the swing of it. I'd say the biggest thing I learned was changing out my tips more frequently and making sure the bottles are all the way open. Other than that everything else was as I expected. The spray stuck to the vertical surfaces very well. The foam really did harden within 30+ seconds. It expanded very well, almost too well in some areas. 

I'd say overall it was a success. I'd like to use another kit in the future for sure and I know I'd be even more successful the next time. But for my first go at it it came out just as I wanted. I'll list a couple Spray Foam kits below for you.

tab_title: This DIY LED Wall Light Is Almost Too Easy
description:
Want a custom LED wall light without building an actual light fixture? In this DIY project, I’ll show you how I made this simple wooden LED wall feature using just two boards and an LED light strip.

Govee LED Light Strip: https://amzn.to/4ylInOV

The build is incredibly simple: a 1x6 gets mounted to the wall with an LED strip running around the outside, then a stained and clear-coated 2x12 is mounted over the front. The hidden LEDs create a floating glow around the board and can completely change the look of the room.

I’ll walk through the entire build step by step, including how I mounted everything, installed the LED strip, finished the wood, and a few things I would do differently if I built it again.

I used an off-brand LED strip for this particular project, but if I were building it again I’d personally go with Govee. I've had better experiences with their lighting products and they offer a lot of options for color-changing LEDs.

Basic materials used:

1x6 board
2x12 board
RGB / color-changing LED strip
Wood stain
Clear coat
Screws / mounting hardware

This is a great DIY project for a bedroom, bunk room, game room, media room, Airbnb, or anywhere you want a unique accent light without installing a traditional wall fixture.

tab_title: How to DIY build a modern deck and pergola using Azek in 15 minutes time-lapse?
description:
I have a 9-5 full time office job like many of you, but it doesn't mean you need to hire someone to transform your backyard into something amazing. Most home improvement projects around the house are DIYable, although some basic skills are required, common sense are far more important. Before you start the project, you need to do enough research, check the bylaws, zoning rules and apply permits (if needed). Most importantly, don't religiously trust all the YouTubers or Facebook videos. 

This video is a time-lapse of what I did in the last 3 years. I am NOT affiliated with any products or companies, my videos for this backyard project are NOT sponsored. I just want to share my experience and made all these videos to help others. There are many tips, trade secrets and technical details I shared with you, hope you find them helpful. Check out the complete list. The backyard project isn't 100% completed, I will continue to upload more in the coming future. 

No Permit Needed?
-------------------------------
Yes, if you check out Part 4 and Part 7 in the video (see below), the city's building inspector came after some neighbors had some concerns. The inspector took some photos and did some measurements, several days after that he told me I DID NOT NEED a permit. So, it is very important to study your local bylaws. 

Cantilever vs Non-cantilever Deck
------------------------------------------------------
To get around the permit, I intentionally designed and built my deck under 2 feet. But the problem is that, I didn't have enough space to have a beam sitting on the post to build a cantilever deck. I say 95% of the decks out there are cantilever. So, I used joist hangers for every single joist, although cost is higher, but permit issue is gone. Check out Part 4 for details.

tab_title: Fix Leaking Shower Head or Bathtub Faucet | Rebuild & Replace Shower Valve
description:
Leaking or dripping bathtub faucet or shower head?  If your shower head or bathtub faucet is leaking or dripping, the shower valve needs to be replaced or needs new seals.  You don't have to replace the shower valve or shower diverter valve because it's easy to rebuild shower stem valves to stop the leak in your bathtub or shower.  If the  bathtub faucet or shower head leaks when the water is off, the valve stem washer needs to be replaced.  If the bathtub faucet or shower head leaks when the water is on, the packing nut needs to be tightened or seal stem packing nut needs to be replaced. 

If you'd like to donate:
https://paypal.me/frugaldiy1

I recommend you go to a plumbing supplier or hardware store to buy valve washers, stem packing seals and shoulder gaskets.  Take your shower valve and diverter valve with you.

tab_title: 5 Energy Bill Mistakes Utility Companies Hope You Keep Making
description:
Go get your last electric bill and look at the number at the bottom. The power company is happy for you to believe that number is the weather, or just the price of things now. It is not. Most of it is five habits scattered through your house that nobody at the utility has any reason to fix, because every one of them lands on their side of the ledger. Mi amigo, not one of these five is a repair. Every fix is free, or twelve dollars.

In this video:
• #1 THE THERMOSTAT is a target, not a gas pedal. Cooling and heating are close to half the bill, and dropping it to 65 does not cool the house faster than 75. It only runs the machine longer
• #2 THE WATER HEATER is about a fifth of the bill and it comes from the factory at 140 degrees. Turn the dial to 120 (breaker off first on an electric tank), and the honest bacteria caveat for a house with a sick, elderly or newborn member
• #3 THE RATE PLAN they never offered you: most utilities have a time-of-use plan where power is far cheaper off-peak. The flat rate is the default because it is easiest for them. You have to call and ask
• Never run the dryer while the house sleeps, even on the cheap rate
• #4 THE ALWAYS-ON TAX: 30 or 40 boxes sipping at once eat 5 to 10 percent of the bill. Cable boxes and consoles in instant-on are the worst. One switched power strip per corner
• What NOT to unplug, and the miracle gadget with the green light that does nothing
• #5 THE TWELVE-DOLLAR PLUG-IN METER that catches your vampire red-handed: the old garage freezer, the spare TV, the surround sound
• Who profits when you do not know: the flat rate, the extra degrees, the glowing boxes, the gadget aisle

I am not a licensed electrician or a licensed anything, and I never claim to be. Turn the breaker off before opening any panel on an electric water heater. If your bill barely moves after all five, the problem is a machine, not a habit, and that is a different conversation.

Tell me in the comments: your state, how old your house is, and once you buy the little meter, what your vampire turned out to be. I read every one.

My wife's channels: Clean The Mexican Way · Cook The Mexican Way
title: 5 Energy Bill Mistakes Utility Companies Hope You Keep Making

tab_title: This Is How We Cool Our House Without AC (The Mexican Way)
description:
You can cool a house with a pipe in the ground. No compressor. No refrigerant. No capacitor that dies in August. Nothing spinning on the side of your house, and no meter spinning inside the wall while it does it. Seventy-four degrees of air coming up out of the dirt on a ninety-six degree afternoon. It has a name — they call it a Canadian well — and it is real, and it is old.

Today I show you exactly how one gets built, what the pipe and fittings actually cost at the yard, and the one thing almost nobody who films these will tell you: the thing that decides whether it cools your house, or grows a mold farm under your yard and pipes it into the room where your family sleeps.

Because there is a version of this that is close to free air conditioning for the rest of your life. And there is a version that is a mistake you sleep in. The difference is TWO NUMBERS you can look up tonight, for free, on the phone in your hand.
title: This Is How We Cool Our House Without AC (The Mexican Way)

1/14/22  It has been about a year since I posted this video. Just so you know, the garage door repairmen who have seen this video and commented don't like this sort of thing. If you have to get your spring replaced, however, from a garage door repairmen, they may charge you more because of the shelves being in their way. tab_title: The Engineering Behind French Drains On An Aquifer (Need A Collab!) 🏡🌪️
description:
Hey everybody, Rob here. After the recent tornado and getting 7 inches of water in my basement, I’ve been doing some serious research on how water moves across my property over the Calumet aquifer. 

In this video, I break down the engineering and theory behind installing shallow 12-to-18-inch French drains to catch and redirect the surface runoff into the lower part of the land before it builds up hydrostatic pressure against the foundation. tab_title: How to Build Shed Doors That Will NEVER Sag (Custom Transom Window Design)
description:
In this video, I’ll show you how to frame, build, and install heavy-duty custom shed doors that will NEVER sag, drag, or twist out of square.

Most kit shed doors use flimsy panels on weak frames that warp after a single season. On this build, we’re building a full 2x4 structural frame locked together with 2.5" GRK structural screws, skinned with LP SmartSide, and reinforced at every corner with 1/2-inch plywood gussets set in Titebond III wood glue and ring shank nails. To give the shed a premium custom look, we added a custom transom window for natural light, finished the exterior with 1x4 white trim, and hung them with heavy-duty black hardware.

tab_title: Can This Backhoe Find My Pond Leak?
description:
Visit our Amazon Affiliate Store:  https://www.amazon.com/shop/indyfarmlife.  This storefront provides links to many of the products we use around the farm.

I’ve been chasing this pond leak for way too long. This time, there’s no more guessing — I’m digging until I find out exactly what’s carrying water away from the pond.

Using the 1987 Case 580K, I dug a trench as deep as 6–7 feet behind the pond dam looking for old clay field tile. At first, I found nothing but water and a whole lot more questions. Then we finally hit clay tile.

From there, the project turned into tracing the old drainage line, figuring out whether it was actually connected to the pond, and removing as much of the 4-inch clay field tile as possible. A pond dye test eventually gave me the confirmation I was looking for.

Of course, nothing around here goes completely according to plan. I nearly lost the backhoe bucket into the trench, the trench filled with water overnight, and then the Case blew a hydraulic line right in the middle of the repair.

Hopefully, after all of this, we’ve finally stopped the leak.

tab_title: PODCAST with video: How RESNET could be better (w/ Trent Fuller)
description:
In this episode of the Structure Talk podcast, Reuben Saltzman and Eric Houseman welcome Trent Fuller to discuss construction-phase inspections, RESNET, and residential energy ratings. They explore how HERS scores help evaluate home energy efficiency, the role of insulation, windows, and blower door testing, and how energy ratings can help builders meet compliance requirements and qualify for Energy Star certification.

Trent shares the challenges inspectors face when implementing new standards, particularly the ACCA 310 HVAC performance verification standard, which can require specialized equipment, training, and additional time. He also introduces the Rater Overhead Impact Index (ROII) initiative, which aims to improve transparency around the time, costs, equipment, and practical demands of new requirements. The discussion highlights the importance of better communication between RESNET and field inspectors to make standards more practical and effective.

Learn More About the ROII Initiative: https://roiiletter.org/ 
Explore Upcoming Inspector Empire Builder Events:
 https://www.iebcoaching.com/events

Takeaways

Construction-phase inspections help identify defects before they are concealed by finished materials.
Third-party inspections help builders maintain quality and reduce liability.
Efficient scheduling and territory management improve inspection team productivity and profitability.
RESNET standards support residential energy ratings and energy code compliance.
HERS scores measure home energy performance and can support ENERGY STAR certification.
Energy ratings consider insulation, windows, solar heat gain, and building orientation.
Window specifications must be documented to verify energy model accuracy.
Blower door tests measure airtightness and help verify air leakage requirements.
ACCA 310 HVAC performance testing can contribute to additional HERS points.
New standards require proper equipment, training, documentation, and field time.
Clear guidance and reliable testing equipment help inspectors produce accurate, defensible results.
Standards should account for implementation costs, administrative work, and operational efficiency.
ROII advocates for greater transparency around the costs and workload of energy rating requirements.
Inspectors should participate in public comments and industry discussions to improve standards.
Better collaboration between standards organizations and field inspectors can strengthen the industry.

tab_title: Teaching My Grandson to Drive a Tractor… and Follow Jesus | Work & The Word
description:
Today at The Lovely Place, my grandson Cayden gets behind the wheel of Big Red, our Case IH 75C tractor, for the very first time!

We've got an overgrown field to cut, a 15-foot Rhino 3150 batwing mower behind us, and a lot of work ahead. But somewhere along the way, this becomes about something much more important than cutting grass.

As Cayden takes the wheel, I talk with him about keeping his eyes on the goal. When you're operating a tractor and trying to cut a straight line, you've got to keep looking toward where you're going.

And isn't life a lot like that?

There are so many things that can distract us, pull us in the wrong direction, or cause us to lose sight of what matters most.

For me, that means keeping my eyes on Jesus and doing my best to walk in the direction He wants me to go.

During our time together, we also talk about something Cayden has been learning from God's Word: *the full armor of God, found in Ephesians 6:10–18.*

The belt of truth.
The breastplate of righteousness.
The shoes of the readiness of the gospel of peace.
The shield of faith.
The helmet of salvation.
The sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God.

And prayer.

These are lessons I hope he'll carry with him long after he's learned how to drive a tractor.

I know not everyone comes to The Lovely Place for the same reasons. Some enjoy the tractors, equipment, land projects, and the progress we're making on our 60+ acres. Others connect with the family stories, faith, and the lessons we're learning along the way.

Today, those things come together.

I'm thankful for the opportunity to spend this time with my grandson, to teach him something new, and to share a little of what matters most to me.

Thanks for spending part of your day with us here at The Lovely Place.

*The work changes. The Word doesn't.*

We’re thankful for every blessing that God provides to each and every one of us. If it’s His will and with His help, we hope to create an off-grid homestead where we can enjoy His creation and live in a way that honors Him. Like many of you, we are not perfect and still have a lot to learn. In our imperfection, we are so thankful for the grace and mercy of God! tab_title: What is the best, most money saving space heater? Infrared, ceramic, mica, oil-filled
description:
Check these affiliate links for the current prices. Mica is my favorite style: https://geni.us/pivquuL (Amazon) 
Mica Panel Heaters: https://geni.us/UIChlW1 (Amazon) || Oil Filled Radiator Heaters: https://geni.us/x0AR (Amazon)  || Ceramic Space Heaters: https://geni.us/DbnBg23 (Amazon)  || Infrared Heaters: https://geni.us/KGLJyL (Amazon) 

Here are the rooms/applications I recommend for the different types of space heaters:

Ceramic Space Heaters: https://geni.us/DbnBg23 (Amazon) - Small ones are good for personal spaces like an office desk or cubicle. Larger ones are good for large rooms like family room, living room, garage etc. The fan can be loud so keep that in mind.

Oil Filled Radiator Heaters: https://geni.us/x0AR (Amazon) - Use this type of space heater in a small to medium sized enclosed room that you are in for long periods of time like a bedroom. It is noiseless and ideal for maintaining a temperature. Good for when you are sleeping.

Infrared Heaters: https://geni.us/KGLJyL (Amazon) - Use these in larger or open areas. Make sure to point it to where people are. These type of heaters often look like furniture so they work well in a living, family, or dining room. They usually have a fan so you will have noise as an issue.

Mica Panel Heaters: https://geni.us/UIChlW1 (Amazon) - Because of its versatility, this is probably my favorite style of space heater. It is noiseless, and lightweight. This will work well for any room and for large open spaces (though a parabolic heater, or heater with a fan is probably a better candidate for open spaces). 

Parabolic Space Heaters: https://geni.us/QKVKHw2 (Amazon) - The room type/size does not really matter much for this; use this for when you don't plan on moving around a lot. Watching TV, working on a workbench, etc (Note: I did not talk about this type of space heater in my video but I did use this type primarily when I was living in China. It is quite bright, so I would use this as a double for a light bulb. It heats up you and not so much the room, so if you move around the room a lot, this probably would not be the recommended style of space heater). 

This is the Amazon list of my favorite space heaters: https://a.co/8UehfTC

The Experiment: Over the course of several months, I tested the room in the morning using various heaters. I tested the increase of temperature over an hour.

The Results: The results were varied and a bit surprising. Basically, the more energy the heater used, the more it would heat the room (I guess that is your basic common sense). I found that heating a room as fast as possible is the best way to minimize cost. The best heater you can get for saving money is the one that gets the room hot the fasted. For me this turned out to be the mica and infrared heaters.

Conclusion: Basically, there is no best heater. You need to find a heater that suits your needs. For me this was the mica heater. This is quiet and hot and was able to heat my room as fast as the infrared heater which is also good. I have seen ceramic heaters that work just as well as this. 

Here is the spreadsheet I used: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/...

A note about the spreadsheet. I used the spreadsheet to organize my data and I don't have all the notes and readings that I originally had; hopefully this spreadsheet helps explain what I was testing though.

tab_title: Water Heater Not Heating? Thermostat Testing Step By Step
description:
Water Heater Not Heating? Testing The Thermostats Step By Step

Water heater not heating? This video shows how to test the thermostats on a water heater. The thermostats or elements are commonly replaced on a water heater that's not heating. The thermostats control the water temperature by turning on the heating elements and maintaining the set temperature. A bad thermostat can cause the water temperature to get to high and trip the reset button which then causes no hot water throughout the home. After shutting off the power to the water heater these tests can be preformed with a multimeter. POWER must be off!

ATTENTION:
What do you do with your old capacitor? Old AC capacitors should never be thrown in the regular trash. Because they store electrical charges and may contain hazardous oils, they require safe handling and specific disposal.

Follow these steps to safely dispose of your capacitor:

1. Safely Discharge It Before handling, the capacitor must be safely discharged.Disconnect: Turn off the power to your AC unit (pull the disconnect box or flip the circuit breaker).Discharge: Take an insulated screwdriver (ensure the handle is rubber or thick plastic). Touch the metal shaft of the screwdriver across the terminals simultaneously (e.g., Common to Fan, then Common to Hermetic). A small spark may occur, rendering the capacitor safe.

2. Take It to a Recycling or Household Hazardous Waste Center.

tab_title: Why is my mini split making noise? It's the bearings.
description:
You Minisplit is noisy because the bearings have gone bad in the blower motor. It is cheap and fairly easy to replace the the bearings and the bearings are very common to find, they are the same bearings used in roller skates and skateboards. The bearings that come in the motors are shielded "608z" bearings. The brand and part number I used are TRITAN "608 2RS PRX" with a barcode number of 2101068647. I would recommend sourcing shielded bearings vs the sealed bearings that I bought. I bought sealed bearings because I was able to go and pick them up the same day and not have to wait on shipping.  

LG mini split heat pump indoor unit models featured in this video are LMN077HVT and LMN157HVT.

Why is my mini split making noise?
How to fix a noisy mini split?

title: Why is my mini split making noise? It's the bearings.

tab_title: Mazda CX-5 Spoiler Rattle / Loose Nut in Hatch — Easy DIY Fix with Loctite
description:
🔧 TOOLS I USED (affiliate links):
👉 10mm Deep Socket: https://link.amazon/B00b7nvNn
👉 Loctite (Blue 242) or similar: https://link.amazon/B03tdoR3C

Hearing a rattle noise in the back of your Mazda CX-5 over bumps? Before you chase interior trim or the cargo area, check the rear spoiler. On the CX-5, the spoiler is held to the liftgate by two studded bolts with 10mm nuts on the inside of the hatch — and one of these nuts can work loose, rattle around inside the door, and let the spoiler itself rattle too. It's one of the most common rattle complaints on these, and it's a quick, cheap fix.

In this video I show you exactly how to find the noise and fix it for good:
✅ How to pop the plastic liftgate panels off carefully (without breaking the clips)
✅ Locating the two studded spoiler bolts and the 10mm nuts
✅ Finding the loose (or dropped) nut that's causing the rattle/noise
✅ Re-tightening with Loctite so it never backs out again
✅ Reinstalling the trim panels cleanly

Total cost: basically free. Total time: about 20 minutes.

TOOLS & SUPPLIES (affiliate):
👉 10mm Deep Socket: https://link.amazon/B00b7nvNn
👉 Ratchet: https://link.amazon/B00b7nvNn
👉 Plastic Pry / Trim Removal Tools: https://link.amazon/B0c6NkMl0
👉 Loctite Threadlocker (Blue) or similar: https://link.amazon/B03tdoR3C

FITMENT:
Confirmed: Mazda CX-5 (1st gen) — 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016
Likely similar (check your vehicle): CX-5 2017–2024, and other Mazda models with a liftgate-mounted rear spoiler may have the same loose-nut rattle — inspect yours before assuming it's identical

tab_title: changing from fuel injection to carburetor,  chevy truck 4.3 engine
description: Fed up with my 1989 chevy truck having trouble so I took off the fuel injection and changed to old school carburetor.  The truck was stalling out and nobody could fix it. So I did it myself even though I am not a mechanic. I found that it is better to install the fuel pump below the gas tank (on the frame), as to get a more solid flow and it kept the pump from getting "vapor lock" and stop pumping. otherwise I had no trouble, I have sense changed to a edelbrock carb, 600 cfm,   I bought it used and rebuilt it. I think now it even runs better and every major auto store has one sitting on the shelf. over a year later I am happy I did it. I am planing to do it to one of my newer cars  2001 hyundi (4 cyl) and am researching how to bypass the computer ignition, and replace it with a stand alone ignition.

description:
After 3½ years of charging three different electric vehicles, it’s time to inspect my Emporia EV charger and the electrical circuit powering it! But how are those electrical connections holding up after years of continuous charging?

In this video, I take you along as I inspect my original DIY EV charger installation, from the 60-amp double-pole breaker inside my electrical load center to the wiring terminals inside the Emporia charger.

I’ll show you All the Steps, including:

⚡ Safely shutting down and checking the electrical circuit

⚡ Inspecting the 6-gauge wiring and ground connections

⚡ Removing and inspecting the 60-amp Square D breaker

⚡ Checking the bus stabs and breaker clips for signs of overheating or damage

⚡ Verifying the manufacturer’s specified terminal screw torque

⚡ Checking 120V and 240V readings at the breaker

⚡ Opening the Emporia EV charger and inspecting its internal wiring connections

⚡ Reassembling everything and checking that the charger is working properly


IMPORTANT ELECTRICAL SAFETY WARNING:

EV charging circuits carry substantial electrical loads. Working inside an electrical load center or EV charger can expose you to dangerous or potentially fatal electrical hazards. Parts of a load center can remain energized even with the main breaker turned OFF.

This video documents my own inspection and is intended for educational purposes. Electrical inspections, testing, and maintenance should be performed by qualified professionals using appropriate safety procedures and properly rated equipment. tab_title: Costco HVAC Replacement Cost 2026: Member Prices & the 10% Shop Card Deal
description:
Costco HVAC replacement in 2026 typically runs $4,000–$8,000 for an air conditioner, $3,000–$7,000 for a furnace, $6,000–$12,000 for a full AC-and-furnace system, and $7,000–$15,000 for a heat pump. Members then receive a Costco Shop Card worth roughly 10–15% of the project cost, bringing effective net costs down to about $5,400–$10,200 for a full system.

Costco partners exclusively with Lennox: you request a consultation online or at the warehouse kiosk, a pre-screened local Lennox dealer performs a one-to-two-hour in-home assessment, sends an itemized quote, and certified technicians usually finish installation in one full day. The Shop Card is mailed two to four weeks after completion and works at any warehouse or online. Executive members stack the annual 2% reward on top — on a $10,000 system, that is $1,000 back on the card plus $200 in Executive rewards.

Fine print: the card is a gift card, not cash, and cannot reduce financing. Ductwork changes ($1,000–$5,000+), electrical panel upgrades ($500–$2,000), and permits ($50–$300) cost extra. Get the free Costco consultation plus two independent quotes, ask which Shop Card promotion is running, and consider the spring or fall off-season when the seasonal discount stacks with the card. tab_title: Furnace and AC Replacement Cost 2026: Full System Prices & Bundle Savings
description:
Replacing your furnace and air conditioner together in 2026 typically costs between $7,000 and $14,000 installed for standard equipment. tab_title: 5 Thermostat Settings That Are Quietly Wrecking Your Furnace This Winter
description:
If your air conditioner has ever kicked on in October, your thermostat is on AUTO, and that's the cheapest of the five settings in this video. The other four sit behind menus most people never open: a hold that kills your schedule, an installer setting that tells the thermostat the wrong furnace, AUX heat set to come on when it isn't needed, and an away temperature lower than your pipes can take. Every one of them takes a few minutes to check.

CHAPTERS
0:00 The air conditioner that came on in October
0:59 What's really inside your thermostat
1:17 #1 AUTO
2:40 #2 The hold button
4:14 #3 The setting the installer picked
5:53 #4 Heat pump owners: AUX heat
7:17 #5 The away temperature
8:41 The five + your week

THIS WEEK
1. Switch the mode from AUTO to HEAT for the season (unless you live where it's hot at noon and cold at night).
2. If the screen says HOLD or PERMANENT HOLD, cancel it and let the schedule run. Seven to ten degrees lower while you sleep. Heat pump? Keep the setback to a couple of degrees.
3. Read the label inside the furnace door (two white plastic vent pipes usually means high-efficiency) and ask your technician to check the thermostat's equipment setting against it.
4. Heat pump owners: on a Nest, set Heat Pump Balance to Balanced or Max Savings. On an ecobee, ask your installer for your balance point and set the AUX heat maximum outdoor temperature to match.
5. Set the away temperature to 55 or higher, check the Nest eco and Safety Temperatures, and open the cabinet doors under sinks on outside walls before you leave.

Tell me in the comments: what state are you in, and is your thermostat on HEAT, AUTO or OFF right now?

SOURCES (named so you can check me)
• Honeywell / Resideo: T6 Pro installation guide and user guide; FocusPRO installation guide (cycle rates); "Thermostat Cycle Rate: What Is It?"
• ecobee: ecobee3 user guide
• Google Nest Help: temperature modes; Heat Pump Balance; Eco Temperatures; Safety Temperatures

SAFETY
Turn the power off at the furnace switch or breaker before you open a furnace door to read the label. If you ever smell gas, leave the house and call your gas company from outside.

tab_title: 5 Thermostat Habits That Are Quietly Wrecking Your Furnace
description:
Your thermostat is the cheapest part of your heating system and the only part you touch every day — which makes it the only place your habits can actually do damage. Five of them, cheapest to fix first, plus the one setting that genuinely saves money.

SOURCES — so you can check me
U.S. Department of Energy — thermostat setback of 7–10°F for 8 hours a day saves up to 10% a year on heating, and 68°F is their recommended winter setting while you're home
U.S. Environmental Protection Agency — Energy Star certification for programmable thermostats was suspended in 2009 after field studies found no measurable savings in real households

IF YOU HAVE A HEAT PUMP
Two things in this video work differently for you. Keep your setbacks small — a few degrees, not ten — because coming back up all at once is what triggers your electric backup heat. And know the difference between AUX heat, which comes on by itself in cold weather and is normal, and EMERGENCY heat, which is a manual switch that shuts your heat pump off entirely and runs the most expensive heat in your house.

THIS WEEK
Change the thermostat batteries. Put the fan switch on AUTO. Set it to 68 and leave it alone. Tape a thermometer next to the thermostat overnight and see what it's really reading. If you have a heat pump, check that the emergency heat switch is off.

Tell me in the comments what state you're in and how old your furnace is. I read every one — the ages tell me more than anything else.

Educational content. If your thermostat is in a sensible spot, your filter is clean, and your furnace is still short cycling, that's a fault and not a habit — get it diagnosed. Gas appliances, flue work and line-voltage wiring are licensed jobs.

Tell me in the comments where you live, whether your radiators sit on outside walls, and roughly how old your house is. I read every one.

Arthur is not a licensed heating technician. This is one homeowner's experience, not professional advice. When in doubt, call a licensed pro.

tab_title: Couple Living Alone Off-Grid on a Tiny Remote Island
description:
Tracy and John bought a tiny 8-acre island in the middle of a freshwater lake in Northern BC for $76k CDN and have been living there full time for over 2 years.  There was a small cabin on on the island that had seen better days and they have been restoring and fixing it up and that's where they live!  The couple has solar power for electricity, they draw water from the lake (and filter it), and they collect their own firewood from the island for heat.  They have a composting toilet and they use propane for cooking and hot water.  Since they live on an island year round in all four seasons, they have an air boat that allows them to get on and off the island in any weather – even during the shoulder seasons when the ice isn't safe to cross any other way.

You can follow and find out more about Tracy and John's Off-Grid Retirement Island here:
   / @iownaisland  

The couple both worked for a charity for most of their lives so they don't have pensions form their employers.  But the low cost of living on the island has allowed them to retire early at 54 and they are self-funding their retirement using some funds from the sale of their house and their retirement savings until they reach 65 and can access old age security and CPP.

They saw many folks never reach retirement age and decided they needed to take the plunge and do what they wanted to do before it was too late.  So far they have no regrets despite some challenges like being far from family, living on a budget, and dealing with intense weather and forest fires.

They are actively setting up their lives so that they can age in place on the island for as long as possible including making the paths safer, and using small machinery like a skid steer to help them with heavy jobs.

You can follow their journey on YouTube here:

This Climate Zone 5A project provides an opportunity to evaluate early high-performance construction details and identify opportunities for improvement. Using 2-D and 3-D drawings, Matt and Steve explore control-layer continuity and the value of redundant protection. They explain how blower door testing during construction provides immediate feedback on air sealing, while positive and negative pressure tests reveal different weaknesses. The discussion also highlights the importance of understanding material vapor permeability, particularly when using closed-cell spray foam. The takeaway: learn from past assemblies to improve future performance.

tab_title: 10 Simple Hacks To Save Heat And Energy Around Your Home
description:
🏠 10 SIMPLE HACKS TO SAVE HEAT AND ENERGY AROUND YOUR HOME 🔥

Most of the heat you pay for doesn't stay in your house. It slips out through gaps, windows, and everyday habits. In this video, a plainspoken older gentleman walks you through 10 cheap, practical ways to keep the warmth in, explaining how heat escapes, why each hack works, what it costs, and what to watch out for. No gadgets, no contractors, just common sense and a few inexpensive supplies.

🪟 THE 10 HACKS COVERED:

Stop drafts under doors (draft stoppers and door sweeps)
Seal gaps around windows and doors (weatherstripping, caulk, and a simple leak test)
Bubble wrap on windows
Open curtains for sun by day, close them at night
Turn the thermostat down a few degrees and heat the person, not the house
Run your ceiling fan in reverse
Cover bare floors with rugs
Put reflective foil behind radiators
Close the doors on rooms you're not using
Check your water heater (temperature, insulation, and pipes)


⚠️ SAFETY NOTES: Savings figures in this video are rough, commonly cited estimates, and real results vary by house and climate. When you make your home tighter, make sure you have working carbon monoxide detectors on every level and near sleeping areas. Don't close too many heating vents or let a closed-off room get cold enough to freeze pipes. Keep bedroom windows usable as emergency exits. If someone in your home is elderly, very young, or unwell, don't let it get uncomfortably cold to save a few dollars. Follow your appliance manuals for water heater and space heater settings.

👍 If this helped you, please hit the like button. It helps other people find simple ways to cut their energy costs.

Stop heat loss in your home with these simple DIY fixes. You can cut your heating bills by up to 10% using these easy methods.

This guide shows you how to properly apply weatherstripping to doors and windows to seal gaps where warmth escapes. tab_title: I found a really easy way to make milky frosted glass for light fixtures
description:
Honestly can't believe this worked so well. SOME NOTES, THOUGH
So I screwed something up with the pour you see here. But actually I'm not entirely sure I did? It looked a bit weird so I inspected it and genius me let the cups fall into the shade and ruined it so I needed to start over again.
When I did, I went just a touch heavier on the glue and also spent more time twirling the bowl around before flipping it over. I got much better coverage, probably because it let the mixture get a little tacky.
However, on the re-pour I decided to try not-at-all with regard to eliminating bubbles and... this was a mistake. You definitely want as few bubbles as possible for best results. Gotta build that vacuum chamber.
Bottom line, this appears to be a pretty decent setup but longevity is TBD. And if you've got some techniques to improve things please share below! But my overall recipe is as follows:

1. Mix equal parts by weight water, acrylic craft paint, and PVA glue. Stir thoroughly but avoid introducing air at all steps.
2. Pour onto inside surface of whatever you're coating. Rotate object for even coverage.
3. Continue rotating for 15 minutes, ensuring every area gets covered multiple times. Mixture should thicken slightly which helps ensure a uniform appearance.
4. Stand object up and let excess drip out, then dry overnight.

Good luck!
title: I found a really easy way to make milky frosted glass for light fixtures

tab_title: We Sold Everything. Here’s What Comes Next
description:
Follow us on    / @thedowntoearthchristian   
After about seven years of building, living off grid, prepping, and sharing our homestead journey with you, this chapter of our lives has come to an end.

We sold our Idaho homestead and are moving out. That also means this will likely be the final video on this channel for quite some time.

But the story of this channel actually began long before Idaho.

We started this YouTube channel in 2013 while living in Indonesia. Back then it was called Riding Java, and I made motorcycle videos while riding around the island of Java. When we returned to the United States, the channel changed along with our lives and eventually became focused on off-grid living, homesteading, preparedness, solar power, and the projects we built here.

Now, Lord willing, Julie and I are preparing to return to Indonesia in about nine months to serve and do mission work.

So in a strange way, we're coming full circle.

I don't know exactly what will happen with this channel, but I'm not deleting it. Once we're settled in Indonesia, I may even get back on a motorcycle and bring back some version of Riding Java.

Most of all, we want to say thank you. Whether you've been here for years or recently found the channel, thank you for watching, commenting, encouraging us, and being part of this journey.

If you enjoy Bible content, discipleship, evangelism, and practical Christian living, I will continue making videos on The Down-to-Earth Christian. Be sure to follow us there.

Thank you for coming along for the ride.

tab_title: I Found Nessmuk's ACTUAL Hatchet! [ Length, Weight, Etc.]
description:
I FOUND NESSMUK'S ORIGINAL HATCHET! After more than 140 years, I had the extraordinary opportunity to examine, photograph, measure, and weigh the original double-bit hatchet preserved by the family of George Washington Sears, better known as Nessmuk!

In this very special episode of Following Nessmuk, I meet with the great-great-great-grandson of George Washington Sears, the legendary outdoorsman and author of the 1884 book Woodcraft.

Not only did I have the opportunity to hold and examine this remarkable piece of outdoor history, but I also conducted an exclusive interview with Nessmuk's descendant, who explains how the hatchet was passed down through the family and eventually given to him by his grandmother.

What makes this discovery so fascinating?

We get an up-close look at the actual double-bit hatchet preserved by the Sears family.

I document its dimensions, cutting edges, distinctive thin profile, and construction.

The complete hatchet weighs just 1 pound, 4.5 ounces!

We examine the wooden handle, believed to be original, and the cord wrapping that was replaced by a later family member.

We hear the family history directly from Nessmuk's great-great-great-grandson.

For generations, bushcraft enthusiasts, outdoorsmen, and knife and axe makers have studied Nessmuk's lightweight camping philosophy and attempted to recreate his famous double-bit hatchet.

Although Nessmuk described his preferred hatchet in Woodcraft, he did not provide detailed measurements or an exact weight. This surviving, family-preserved example offers a fascinating opportunity to study the dimensions and construction of the real thing.

Join me for one of the most memorable episodes of Following Nessmuk as we explore an extraordinary surviving piece of American outdoor history.

tab_title: STOP Wasting your FireWood ASH! LEARN what we use it for...
description:
#homestead #firewood 
We end up with barrels and barrels of wood ash during the burning season, but there are so many things you can use the ASH for. In today's video learn what we use wood ash for on our homestead. 

Clean Wood Stove Window
Mix some ash with some water and create a paste.  It becomes an abrasive cleaner to clean your window.  It works surprisingly well

Cleaning Oil Spills
Ash can absorb oil spills just like kitty litter can.  My husband does all of our car work in our garage and we sometimes get oil spills on the ground, we have been using some cheap cat litter, but why not use what we have on hand and what is for free?  By sprinkling wood ash onto an oil spill, it will absorb the oil and allow for an easy cleanup with an outdoor broom and dustpan.
Repairing ruts in driveway

Eliminate orders in Fridge/Freezer
I use baking soda to absorb odors in my fridge, but I just found out that putting a cup or so of ash in a bowl or even a mason jar towards the back will do the same trick as the baking soda.

Natural Ice Melt
Did you know you can use ash as a way to melt ice on your driveway or walkway?  There are natural minerals in the wood ash that help melt ice.  Just be careful if you put it close to your house when entering, it would easily come into your house from your shoes. 


Fertilize Gardens
If you create a circle of wood ash around your crops this will prevent slugs and snails from crossing into your plant beds.  Or dump a bucket on your garden
Dust Bath for Poultry
I have so much sand here on our homestead, but I just found out that ash helps treat fleas and other insects, it’s perfect for helping poultry relieve themselves of parasites.  Chickens naturally dust bath to help clean their feathers of pesky bugs but give your girls an extra boost by adding some ash to their dust area.

tab_title: The $30 Tool That Gets Water Out When Your Pump DIES
description:
🔗 Save $6,000 A Year with My Complete Amish Home-Saving Method I teach:
https://eliasyoder.com

The power goes out here for three days every few winters, and by the second morning there are neighbours in my lane with buckets. They are welcome to the water. But what I tell every one of them is that they have more water than I have, and they are standing on top of it.

Your well is not dry. Your pump is off. Those are two different problems and only one of them is yours this week. There is a column of water down that casing that has not moved an inch since Tuesday, and you can get it out with a length of pipe, a cap, a rubber ball and a rope, for about thirty dollars.

I also owe you a correction in this one. I have said in a few videos that this method draws a bucket a minute all day long. That depends entirely on one number I never mentioned, and on a deep well it makes a liar of me. The real figures are in here.

What is in this one:

Why the well and the pump are two separate things My grandfather, a length of galvanised pipe on a nail, and the two days I spent carrying water up a hill for nothing The first number you need, which is not how deep your well is How to measure your static water level yourself in ten minutes with a capped pipe and a marked line Where to get your well completion report The second number, the inside of your casing, and why the pump, drop pipe and cable have already taken up the room Why a four inch casing wants an inch and a half bailer and a six inch will take two or three The thirty dollar build, part by part Why the vent hole in the top cap is the difference between working and not The ball check and how it seals, and when to spend the extra on a brass foot valve What each size actually holds, and what five gallons costs you in minutes at twenty five, a hundred and two hundred feet What a household actually needs per day, and the one job this will not do Why you run the rope over a bar and not over the bare casing rim Hauling hand over hand, gloves, and why you should not coil on every trip Why you build this in October and test it once in daylight Deep well hand pumps, and why the forty dollar pitcher pump will do nothing on most drilled wells Why nobody talks about a thirty dollar pipe when a generator has an advertising budget

SAFETY, please read this part. Turn the breaker off for the pump before the cover comes off and leave it off. Look hard at what the cap is holding before loosening anything, because on some wells the whole weight of the pump hangs from the top plate and unbolting it drops the pump down the well. Tie the rope with a bowline and a stopper knot and tug it hard before it goes down, because a bailer that comes off the line can jam beside the drop pipe and leave you with a well you can neither pump nor bail. Let nothing uncontrolled pass over an open casing, including tools, glasses and telephones. Never reach down a well and never get into one, because a casing is a confined space and the air at the bottom is not always air.

That cap is sealed to keep your water clean, and opening it is the likeliest way anybody contaminates their own well. Wipe the bailer and the whole rope with a weak bleach solution first, coil the rope on a clean board and never on the ground, keep the hole covered when you are not drawing, and cap it properly the moment you finish. Then treat what you draw as suspect and boil or disinfect it. The exact bleach measures are in the emergency water video.

If your well sits in sand or silt you will draw cloudy water, so let it settle and pour off the clear. If your ground has flooded or you have any reason to think the well is contaminated, do not use this method at all.

I am Elias Yoder. I farm in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania.

tab_title: KILL EVERY Mosquito The AMISH Way. SAFE For Honey Bees & Pets!
description:
My name is Elias Yoda. I am Amish. I keep eleven hives of honeybees on this farm, my wife tends a half-acre of flowers and herbs the pollinators depend on, and I have not been bitten by a mosquito at my own kitchen table in nine years.
No bug zapper. No spray truck. No chemical company on retainer. And every female mosquito within a hundred yards of my farmhouse is, right now, flying toward a five-gallon bucket behind my woodshed to lay eggs that will be dead within twenty-four hours.
In this video, I am going to walk you through exactly what I do, in the order I do it, for less than the cost of one professional spray treatment. You will learn the bucket-and-bits trick that handles the eggs at the source, the essential oil spray that takes care of the adults, the source reduction walk my grandfather did every Saturday morning, and the smudge can my grandmother lit at dusk on the porch. Every bit of it is safe for honeybees, butterflies, dogs, chickens, songbirds, and children. None of it requires electricity. None of it requires a contract.
I am also going to tell you the part that might make you uneasy — which is that the lawn care companies in your town have known about the safe option for forty years, and most of them still spray your yard with something that kills the honeybees right along with the mosquitoes. The reason is simple, and I will explain it.
Mosquitoes kill more people every year than any other animal on earth. This is serious business. But the way most of the country has been told to handle the problem is not the only way, it is not even the best way, it is just the way somebody makes money from. The honeybee population in this country is in trouble, and the same chemicals being used to kill mosquitoes in suburban yards are part of the reason. You can do better. We always have.
Walk your property this weekend with a coffee can. Put out three buckets in hidden corners. Tell me in the comments where you live and what your mosquito situation is like right now. I read every one of them. And tell me if you put out a bucket. I want to hear how it goes.
Next video: what my grandmother used to do to keep flies out of the kitchen in August, using a glass jar, a piece of paper, and one ingredient from the pantry you would never guess. It worked for a hundred years before sticky paper was invented and it still works better than anything you can buy. Subscribe so you do not miss it.

➡️➡️ GET MY COOKBOOK: www.homesteadcookbook.com

EASY BREAD RECIPE: 

1 1/3 cup warm water (100-110*F)
2 teaspoons active, dry yeast
2 teaspoons brown sugar or honey
1 egg
1 teaspoon fine sea salt
3 to 3 1/2 cups all-purpose flour

In a large mixing bowl, combine the water, yeast, and sugar.

Stir until dissolved, then add in the egg and salt.

Add the flour one cup at a time. Once the mixture is too stiff to mix with a fork, transferred it to a well-floured countertop.

Knead for 4-5 minutes, or until smooth and elastic. Add more flour if the dough is continues to stick to your hands.

Shape the smooth dough into a ball and place in a bowl. Cover with a dish cloth and let rise in a warm place for one hour (or until the dough has doubled).

Grease a standard-sized loaf pan (9"x5"). After the first rise is complete, punch down the dough and shape it into a "log". Place it into the loaf pan and allow to rise 20-30 more minutes, or until it starts to peek over the edge of the pan. Bake in a 350* oven for 25-30 minutes, or until lightly browned.

tab_title: How to Expand Your Wireless Range Using an Old Router
description:
Check out this video to learn how to configure an old router to expand the wireless in your home, garage, pole barn, or greenhouse. I have used this process for many years both professionally and in my own home. This is a great use for that older router that you may have replaced with a new one or picked up from a garage sale or resale shop. Routers have become almost disposable after a few years so they come cheap. The newer routers will offer a better wireless extension and also better security so if you can find one that is at least 2007 or newer that is preferred. 

Using an old router to expand your network is a cheap and easy way to at least double the wireless range in your home. It is also a great way to get wireless to outbuildings or other areas that are outside of your home's wireless signal. This method does require that you have an Ethernet cable run from your main wireless router in your home to the location where you would like to setup the second router (access point). In our home I have one wireless access point configured on each floor and staggered from one end of the home to the other. This means that no matter where I ma in the house I can always connect to a nearby access point and have full signal strength. No buffering, no lag, and in most cases speeds as fast as a wired Ethernet connection. 

Here are the basic steps to follow but I would recommend watching the accompanying video to fully understand the process.

1. Reset router to factory default settings
2. Take note of your current network configuration (192.168.1.X
3. Create a new ip address for the access point 192.168.1.220 (example)
4. plug a computer into the newly reset router
5. log into the router using the default ip - normally 192.168.1.1
6. Configure the wireless network name and security
7. Turn off DHCP (take away the router's ability to assign ip addresses)
8. Configure the router to the previously picked ip address - 192.168.1.220 (example)
9. Connect the router to an Ethernet cable coming from your main router. 

Tip - Do not use the "WAN" port at all on this new access point. 

     Now I know that someone is going to say it so I will answer this question up front. Yes, you can just plug the router into your existing setup using the WAN port on the second router without changing any settings on the router. This will work in most cases however you are setting yourself up for problems down the road as this is not the correct way to configure a second wireless router on an existing network. This is what is called double NAT or network address translation and is like having a double firewall. This will not allow any computers connected to the secondary router to communicate with wireless printers, other computers, will block many gaming sites, vpn's and other connections. Although it is easier and may work for basic internet browsing it will be slower and will cause other issues down the road.

description:
this is the one for the people who want the smallest and lightest, full-power DIY solar dish cooker. this "mini version" of my original works awesome. boils bakes and fries. feeds 1 to 2 people. works with 6-to-8-inch pans. its small size makes it super convenient for an "on the go" or "adventure" lifestyle (camping, rv life etc.) or for everyday use at home. all the cooking shown in the video was done in mid-December 2025. it works so well, that it may end up being my "main unit". video includes the full build plus how to make the pot stand. the build portion of the video starts around 3:58

to see the standard and super size models check out my last 2 videos. those show the 40" family size version and the 36" standard size model. all three are loosely based on a professional model that is no longer sold. links are listed below. currently there are no "shallow dish" parabolic solar cookers on the market. the only parabolic dish cookers being sold these days are the oversized and overpowered "deep dish" ones. but those units are ridiculously large and heavy (5 ft wide and 33 lbs.) and generate 2 to 3 times the power that you need for everyday cooking, so they are totally unsuitable for most people.  

a note about the mini model: i wouldn't recommend making it any smaller than 30". if you make it any smaller it won't generate the power needed to cook full meals. the theoretical power of a 30" unit is 456w. with its realistic power being 330-360w. just enough for eggs burgers grilled cheeses and boiling small pots of water

all three units are very easy to make; all are tripod mountable and all should last for years. (if you don't get them wet). that's essentially there only weakness. and if you really want to go 'the extra mile' you can somewhat waterproof cardboard by using shellac. I've looked into all other available materials for construction, but nothing even comes close to cardboard in terms of cost, feasibility, availability, and practicality.
