Strong hvac technician sales performance depends on clear communication, not simply knowing how to close. Developing hvac technician skills means learning to translate technical information into explanations homeowners can follow. In hvac sales, confusion creates uncertainty, hesitation, and objections that could have been avoided.

scott sylvan bell uses an experience with an unfamiliar rental car in Tampa to demonstrate how customers feel when confronted with unfamiliar equipment. Even simple controls became difficult to understand because their locations and functions were different from what he expected. hvac service training videos can teach technical concepts, but hvac service technician sales training must also teach technicians how to explain those concepts from the customer's perspective.

Improving hvac service techncian skills requires simplifying explanations before presenting repair or replacement options. An hvac tech set lead can be lost when a technician overwhelms a homeowner with technical terminology instead of creating understanding. Through sellingtechnicians.com, the emphasis is on developing communication processes that help technicians explain equipment confidently and professionally.

hvac sales training videos from @hvactechsecrets and scott808 provide free hvac sales training focused on practical communication. Working with an hvac sales training expert can help technicians recognize when their explanations create confusion rather than clarity.

Why You Lose Clients When Explaining HVAC Parts To Homeowners examines how technical language can unintentionally create sales objections. Scott recommends reducing explanations to one, two, or three sentences whenever possible. Technicians should record themselves explaining equipment and ask someone outside the HVAC industry whether the explanation makes sense.

Learning how to explain hvac systems also involves using comparisons, analogies, and visual demonstrations. A homeowner should not need technical training to understand why a component matters, what the technician discovered, or which options are available. The objective is to reduce uncertainty and establish confidence through understanding.

Recognizing where you lose hvac sales often starts before the closing conversation. Scott's Tech Set Blueprint addresses the communication skills that help technicians explain parts, present recommendations, and establish professional credibility. tab_title: Lennox Central Air Conditioner - What You Should Know Before Buying!
description:
D-Air Conditioning Website
https://d-airconditioning.com/pages/a...

Instagram
  / d_air_conditioning  

Lennox is one of the most popular brands for central heating and air conditioning. In this video, we will go over the air conditioning offerings by Lennox. The goal of this video is to demystify the products available so that you as the homeowner can make a better decision. Let’s get started.

Here I am at the Lennox website. We will start by going to the homeowner's solutions. One thing that you will find out about Lennox is that they have a lot of products.Twelve air conditioners to be more precise.

Lennox has three lines for their products. Merit, Elite, and Signature. The Merit line is the most affordable. They are the standard level for central air conditioning. The Elite line the mid-tier products. They offer great features at reasonable prices. The Signature line is the Rolls Royce of central air conditioners. For those that can afford the signature and want the very best of the best products available, this is the line for them.

Lennox produces all of their Elite and Signature products in the United States. The Merit line is made in Mexico and so the cost is a bit lower.

The first model in the Merit line is the 13ACX. This is the entry level product for Lennox. In California, this product is not available because of the SEER level. California requires a minimum of 14 SEER. This product is available in other states. You will notice that this model is a single stage operation. This means that the system will turn full power to reach the desired cooling temperature. Once the temperature is reached, it will turn off. It will turn on again when needed. With the single stage system, you will get the cooling you need. You just have to deal with the noise of the system turning on and off.

The ML14XC1 is a single stage system. It is similar to the 13ACX model. The only difference is the SEER rating. This system is designed to be 14 SEER but depending upon the configuration, you can get up to 17 SEERs.

The 16ACX model is the least expensive two stage system that Lennox offers. A two stage system has two motors. When you first turn it on, it will go full power. When the temperature is reached, it will turn off half of its power and coast along. The benefit of a two stage system is that it does not turn on and off. This leads to a much lower noise level than a single stage system. This particular model is rated at 16 to 17 SEERs.

The XC13 and the EL16XC1 models are both single stage air conditioners. The Elite line has better insulation on the compressor outside than the Merit line. As a result, the noise level is much lower. The main difference between these two systems is the SEER rating. The EL16XC1 is the model that we sell the most. It has the perfect balance between noise level, SEER rating, and price. We believe that this is the best value for money product that Lennox offers.

The EL18XCV is a new model from Lennox. It is the first truly variable speed air conditioner available in the Elite line. A single stage system has one motor that turns on and off. A two stage system has two motors that can turn on full power or coast at half speed. Using this same analogy a variable system has 50 different modes. So if you need 9% you can get 9%. If you need 70%, the unit will produce precisely the cooling that you need. A single stage system will cool your house but the temperature indoors can differ from the thermostat by 3 to 5 degrees. A two system system will have a difference of 2 to 3 degrees. A variable system will give you precise temperature within 1 degree.

Lennox is the most recognizable brand for central heating and air conditioning in the United States. If you go to Costco or Home Depot, you will see them present the Lennox system. This is a solid HVAC system and is on the higher side in terms of cost relative to the rest of the market. Lennox dealers are well trained and they are highly selective on who can be a Lennox Premier dealer. The number of people with access to the signature line is limited to ensure quality of the technicians as well as exclusivity.

If you are in the market for a Lennox system and you live in California, please consider working with us. D Air Conditioning company has been working with Lennox for nearly a decade and we offer high quality installation at reasonable prices. We have retail locations in both Southern California and Northern California. Our Socal office is located in Orange County and we service San Diego, Orange County, and LA. Our Norcal office is located in San Jose and we service the SF Bay Area and Sacramento. If you have any questions, please give us a call or send us an email. Our team is happy to answer any and all questions that you have about air conditioning. You can get a free estimate by using the form below.
title: Lennox Central Air Conditioner - What You Should Know Before Buying!

tab_title: Your AC Is Buzzing? Don’t Ignore This Contactor Problem
description:
That buzzing sound coming from your outdoor AC unit could be warning you about a failing contactor, and ignoring it could eventually put your compressor at risk.

In this HVAC training video, we walk through a real service call where a worn contactor is struggling to make a solid electrical connection. You’ll see the carbon tracking and heat damage firsthand, learn why the contactor starts buzzing, and watch the proper process for replacing it.

We also cover:

• How to verify power is actually off before touching the unit
• Why 24V control voltage still matters
• How an HVAC contactor actually works
• What carbon buildup does to electrical contacts
• Why voltage drop can become a bigger problem
• How to label wires before removing a contactor
• Line voltage vs. control voltage
• How anti-short-cycle protection works
• Why you should always double-check your wiring
• How ants can actually damage an HVAC contactor
• Common mistakes that can blow a fuse or even damage a transformer

Whether you're a new HVAC technician, learning the trade, or just want to understand what’s happening inside an air conditioner, this is a simple repair with some important lessons behind it.

⚠️ HVAC equipment contains dangerous high voltage. This video is for educational purposes. Always disconnect and verify power before servicing electrical equipment.

In today's HVAC AO video, I respond to a service call involving a 7-month-old Carrier Infinity 59MN7 furnace that has been nothing but trouble for the homeowner.

The original installing contractor reportedly returned approximately 8 TIMES trying to resolve recurring high-limit lockouts without success.

A second HVAC contractor was called in, but after admitting they weren't familiar with the Infinity system, they installed a basic thermostat, leaving the homeowner without the communicating configuration she originally paid for.

That's where I come in! 🔧

I perform my own troubleshooting, inspect the system, and contact Carrier technical support to confirm my findings and the necessary repairs and adjustments.

But things take an unexpected turn when I explain the cost of the additional services. The homeowner becomes frustrated, calls me a SCAMMER, and declines the work.

And believe me, I understand her frustration. After spending thousands of dollars and dealing with multiple contractors, I can understand why she has lost trust.

But here's the question: Should HVAC technicians be expected to perform additional services for free because previous contractors couldn't resolve the problem?

Why do Chillers, AHUs, Cooling Towers, Pumps, and other HVAC equipment fail unexpectedly?
In many cases, HVAC failures are not actually sudden. Equipment often provides warning signs weeks or months before a major breakdown—such as dirty filters, high motor current, abnormal vibration, refrigerant leakage, loose electrical connections, poor airflow, and abnormal temperatures.
The key is identifying these warning signs and taking action before they become expensive failures.

description:
Is your air conditioner struggling to keep your home cool? ☀️🥵 The culprit might be hiding in plain sight. In this video, we’re showing you exactly how to clean your AC condenser coils to restore your system's cooling power and save money on your monthly energy bills.

When your outdoor unit is covered in dirt, pollen, grass clippings, or pet hair, it can't release heat efficiently. This forces your compressor to work twice as hard, leading to higher bills and eventual system failure. We’ll walk you through the entire process, from the safety basics to the best cleaning solutions to use.

In this step-by-step DIY tutorial, we cover:

Safety First: How to properly shut off the power at the "disconnect box" to avoid electrical hazards.

The Right Tools: Why you should avoid pressure washers and what to use instead (hint: a standard garden hose is your best friend).

Cleaning Solutions: When to use plain water vs. specialized "coil cleaner" foams, and a DIY alternative.

The Technique: How to spray the coils without bending the delicate aluminum fins.

Straightening Fins: A quick look at using a "fin comb" to repair existing damage for maximum airflow.

Final Inspection: What to look for before turning the power back on.

A clean condenser can improve your AC’s efficiency by up to 30%! Don’t pay a technician $200 for a service you can easily do yourself with a garden hose.

tab_title: Gas Safety Week: Carbon Monoxide Safety Checks Every Home Should Know
description:
Gas Safety Week is an important reminder to Take No Chances with gas appliances, boiler safety and carbon monoxide.

In this video, Cindy and Aimee from WarmZilla talk through practical gas-safety checks every household should know. They discuss where carbon monoxide can come from, possible warning signs, how CO alarms work and what to do if an alarm sounds.

Carbon monoxide cannot be seen, smelt or tasted, so you cannot rely on your senses to detect it. A suitable, working carbon monoxide alarm provides an essential warning — but it should never replace regular appliance maintenance and annual boiler servicing.

⚠️ Important safety note: This is an informal conversation based on our experiences as homeowners and renters, supported by general gas-safety guidance. It is not a substitute for advice from a Gas Safe registered engineer or medical professional. Never attempt gas work yourself. If you suspect a gas or carbon monoxide leak, leave the property immediately and follow the emergency guidance below.

In this video:

00:00 – Introduction to Gas Safety Week and “Take No Chances”  
01:43 – Portable heaters and camping risks  
03:01 – How carbon monoxide is detected  
03:50 – Installing a carbon monoxide alarm  
05:18 – Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning  
07:59 – Fuel-burning and electric heaters  
08:41 – Boiler maintenance and annual servicing  
10:03 – Boiler warning signs and personal experiences  
12:43 – Smoke alarms vs carbon monoxide alarms  
14:13 – Alarms for people who are deaf or hard of hearing  
14:31 – What to do if your CO alarm sounds  
18:49 – The five-point gas-safety checklist  

Carbon monoxide can be produced by faulty, incorrectly installed or poorly maintained fuel-burning appliances, including those that use gas, oil, wood, coal, paraffin or LPG.

Standard electric heaters do not produce carbon monoxide because they do not burn fuel. However, they can still present electrical and fire risks if they are damaged or used incorrectly.

⚠️ What should you do if your carbon monoxide alarm sounds?

• Stop using any appliance you think may be responsible, if it is safe to do so  
• Open doors and windows as you leave  
• Get everyone outside into fresh air  
• Do not return until you have received professional advice  
• If you suspect a gas appliance, call the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999  
• If anyone feels unwell, call NHS 111 for medical advice  
• Call 999 if someone is struggling to breathe, suddenly confused, unconscious or seriously unwell  

Never ignore a carbon monoxide alarm and never attempt DIY gas work.

tab_title: Dirty Furnace Filter? What a $5 Part Is Doing to Your Furnace
description:
Your furnace filter is one of the cheapest parts in your house, and when it plugs up it quietly beats up a furnace that cost you thousands.  Here's what a dirty filter actually does, what it doesn't do, and how to change it the right way.

What you need to know:
A plugged filter cuts airflow across the heat exchanger.  The furnace runs hot, the high limit safety switch shuts the burners off, and you get short cycling.
That limit switch isn't built to cycle all day, and manufacturers warn that dirty filters can shorten the life of the heat exchanger.
Newer variable speed blowers ramp up to push through a dirty filter and use more power doing it.  Enbridge says a dirty filter also increases your natural gas use.
In summer, low airflow can let your AC coil ice up.
A dirty filter is NOT proof your heat exchanger is cracked.  If someone says it is, ask them to show you.
Natural Resources Canada and Enbridge: change it at least every three months.  ENERGY STAR: check it every month, especially in winter and summer.
The airflow arrow points toward the furnace.  Never run the furnace without a filter.

In this video:
What a plugged filter does to your furnace in winter
The heat exchanger question, answered honestly
Why newer blowers and your gas bill both pay for a dirty filter
What a dirty filter does to your AC in summer
How to change a filter the right way (size, arrow, no-filter mistake)
How to pick a filter, and why a higher rating isn't always better
How often to check and change it

Chapters:

description:
What does a heat pump actually look like after a year of British weather? In Part 1 of our annual service series, we take the outdoor unit apart to find out.

We're back at a property in Stockport for the first annual service on a 7kW Vaillant aroTHERM plus we installed just over 12 months ago. The customer has reported no issues since install, so this is a routine service: we strip the outdoor unit down, clean it properly, check it over and put it back together exactly as we found it.

Annual servicing isn't just about keeping things tidy. It's a condition of the manufacturer's warranty, and keeping the coil, fan and drain clear helps the system keep performing the way it was designed to.

WHAT WE COVER IN PART 1:
Why Vaillant require an annual service to keep your warranty valid
Why we never use a drill or any ignition source when stripping the unit down
Cleaning the coil fins front and back without damaging them
Why a clogged fan and air intake reduce performance
The 250mm clearance rule for airflow behind the unit
Flushing the condensate tray and checking the drain is clear
Why every single screw matters when it goes back together

tab_title: I Added COOLING to My Vaillant Heat Pump… What Happened?
description:

In this video, I take you through the whole process from start to finish.

I fit the cooling chip to my Vaillant aroTHERM plus, show you where it goes, then go through the settings needed to enable cooling.

But… it doesn’t work first time! 😬

I end up having to do a factory reset and some fault finding before finally getting the cooling system working.

Once it’s running, I use my underfloor heating as the cooling emitter and even experiment with fans blowing across the floor to help move the cooled air around the house.

I then compare the temperatures in the house with the temperatures we’ve experienced during the recent heatwave to see just how effective the Vaillant cooling actually is.

So is cooling on a Vaillant aroTHERM plus genuinely useful, or is it just a gimmick?

Since the old oil system was providing hot water Ken set up a temporary system, using 5 gallon buckets of oil, to keep the 2 boilers running so the families would have hot water through the course of the project.
The first floor apartment of the house had gas, but just for cooking. The gas company came and installed a second meter.
The two existing hot water tanks were in good condition and have lifetime warranties so there was no need to replace them. 
The project went smoothly, inspections were done, all old equipment and debris was removed. The households are now enjoying safe efficient gas heat. They will enjoy it even more in the heating seasons when they fully realize the savings on their energy bills as a result of converting from oil to gas.

description:
An overview of what’s involved in routine air conditioning preventative maintenance.

Preventative maintenance is essential for keeping your central air conditioning system running efficiently, preventing unexpected summer breakdowns, and extending the lifespan of your equipment. In this video, we cover the core inspection points, cleaning procedures, and operational checks completed during a standard AC tune-up.

Key Checklist Items Featured:
Air Filter & Airflow Check: Inspecting filter condition and checking system static pressure.
Condenser Coil Cleaning: Removing dirt, leaves, and debris buildup from outdoor coils.
Electrical Component Testing: Checking capacitors, contactors, wiring connections, and voltage.
Drain Line & Pan Maintenance: Flushing the condensate drain line to prevent clogs and water damage.
Refrigerant & Blower Inspection: Checking system pressures, temperatures, and blower assembly condition.

Why Routine AC Maintenance Matters:
Regular maintenance helps ensure your cooling system operates at peak energy efficiency, maintains optimal indoor humidity control, and catches small component wear before it leads to costly emergency repairs.
